title: Introduce holistic seq-mosaic runner and affinity heatmap serializer
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: our existing benchmark runners focus on either long-horizon sequences or short-burst traffic; they do not faithfully reproduce real production mixes where clients interleave short prompts, mid-length context completions, and occasional long document generations within the same session. This PR adds a new 'seq-mosaic' workload runner that synthesizes a realistic per-session mosaic of sequence lengths and token distributions and couples it with an Affinity Heatmap Serializer that produces compact per-kernel 'richness' telemetry suitable for offline analysis. Design summary: 1) session generator: builds sessions from configurable distributions (short/mid/long proportions, inter-arrival jitter, user intent switch probability); 2) primer manager: issues deterministic priming sequences with probabilistic dropout to emulate KV-cache churn; 3) affinity-aware scheduler: emits labels for token spans denoting likely kernel hotpaths (soft affinity) for downstream attribution; 4) heatmap serializer: encodes per-batch/kernel coverage and token-density histograms into a compact ND-JSON-friendly blob with versioning. Compatibility: runnable as a standalone benchmark process or as a plugin to the existing run-coordinator. Includes an opt-in deterministic mode (seeded RNG) for reproducible profiling. Checklist: - [x] Implement session mosaic generator - [x] Integrate primer manager with kv-cache priming hooks - [x] Produce affinity labels on token boundaries - [x] Serialize heatmaps into compact ND-JSON lines - [x] Add unit tests for sampler statistics - [x] Add integration test with run-coordinator - [x] Add docs and quickstart config Example results (local 8xA10 cluster, 64 concurrency synthetic mix): - median p95 token latency improvement observed in prior-prefetch baseline: none (control) - seq-mosaic baseline end-to-end P95: 183ms - with primer-manager prefetch enabled: P95 -> 141ms (-23%) - kernel-richness heatmap size per 5k requests: ~48KB (gzipped) - example affinity precision@k=100: 0.72 Notes and considerations: this runner intentionally trades off some absolute throughput for fidelity in sequence transitions and kvcache churn; it is intended for regression and saturation experiments where realism of interleaved sequence lengths is valued. The PR also includes a small shim to translate older heatmap outputs into the new versioned schema for backwards compatibility.

review_comments: Liam O'Connor: This looks great from a design perspective. A couple of perf questions: can the sampler run in a low-memory mode and do we have any backpressure safety if the primer manager saturates the prefetch queue?

Aisha Patel: Great points. Sampler supports a 'compact' mode that streams events instead of materializing full sessions; primer manager exposes a max_prefetch_tokens setting and will stop issuing primers if queue depth exceeds threshold. Added tests for that behavior in test_seq_mosaic_sampler.py
Mei Chen: Can we add an opt-out flag for the affinity label emission to avoid extra overhead in pure throughput runs?
Aisha Patel: Added 'emit_affinity' boolean in config and guarded expensive bookkeeping behind it; default remains true for fidelity runs
Ravi Kapoor: CI reported an intermittent serialization failure when running on Python 3.11 matrix; looks like a datetime formatting mismatch in heatmap_serializer.py
Aisha Patel: Fixed serializer to use isoformat with timespec='milliseconds'; added matrix test and retriggered CI
